title: Effect of Gastric Electrical Stimulation on Serum Insulin Levels
official: Defining the Effect of Gastric Electrical Stimulation on Serum Insulin Levels in Human Subjects
summary: The goal of this study is to determine how much effect turning off an individual's Gastric Electrical Stimulator (GES) for up to four hours will have on levels of insulin, C-peptide, GLP-1 and glucose levels.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* At least 18 years of age.
* Documented diagnosis of gastroparesis
* Not taking diabetic prescribed exogenous insulin.
* Patient has a GES device that has been implanted for at least 3 months.
* Willing to give up to 8 blood samples.
* Willing to lie in a bed for up to 5.5 hours.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnancy
* History of allergic reaction to EKG lead placement adhesives.
* Unable to give informed consent.
* Unwilling to give up to 8 5 ml blood samples.
* Unwilling to lie in a bed for up to 5.5 hours.
